SIKADUR®-330: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikadur®-330, May 2023, Version 04.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/sikadur_-330.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikadur®-330 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02).
1.2 Product description. Sikadur®-330 is a 2-component, thixotropic epoxy based impregnating resin and adhesive.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikadur®-330 may only be used by experienced professionals. Sikadur®-330 is used as:
    - Impregnation resin for SikaWrap® fabric reinforcement for the dry application method
    - Primer resin for the wet application system
    - Structural adhesive for bonding Sika® CarboDur® plates into slits
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikadur®-330
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-component epoxy impregnation resin for SikaWrap CFRP systems and Near Surface Mounted CFRP
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v4 MRc 4 (Option 2): Building Product Disclosure and Optimization - Material Ingredients
    - Conformity with LEED v2009 IEQc 4.1: Low-Emitting Materials - Adhesives and Sealants
    - VOC-SCAQMD Method 304-91
2.3 Approvals / certificates.
    - Avis Technique N° 3/16-875 (annule et remplace N° 3/10-669) Sika® CarboDur®, SikaWrap®
    - CIT n°290 18/07/2017 (certificato di idoneità tecnica all'impiego) ; Sika ® CarboDur®, SikaWrap®, Sikadur®
    - Road and Bridges Research Institute (Poland): IBDiM No AT/2008-03-336/1
    - Adhesive for structural bonding tested according to EN 1504-4, provided with the CE-mark
    - VOC-SCAQMD Method 304-91
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-4: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN 1465: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in flexure (p.2).
    - ISO 527: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strain at break (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1770: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Coefficient of thermal expansion (p.2).
    - EN 12614: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.2).
    - ASTM D3418: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Glass transition temperature (p.2).
    - ASTM D 648: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Heat deflection temperature (p.2).
    - EN ISO 9514: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Pot Life (p.3).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy mix and application by trowel and impregnation roller
    - Manufactured for manual saturation methods
    - Excellent application behaviour to vertical and overhead surfaces
    - Good adhesion to many substrates
    - High mechanical properties
    - No separate primer required
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Colour: Component A: white paste; Component B: grey paste; Components A + B mixed: light grey paste
    - Density: 1.30 ± 0.1 kg/l (component A+B mixed) (at +23 °C)
2.7 Viscosity. Shear rate: 50 /s
    | Temperature | Viscosity |
    | +10 °C | ~10 000 mPas |
    | +23 °C | ~  6 000 mPas |
    | +35 °C | ~  5 000 mPas |
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 3 800 N/mm² (7 days at +23 °C) (DIN EN 1465)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 30 N/mm² (7 days at +23°C) (ISO 527)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 4 500 N/mm² (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.9 % (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Concrete fracture (> 4 N/mm²) on sandblasted substrate (EN ISO 4624)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 4.5 × 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temperature range −10 °C − +40 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Service temperature: –40 °C to +45 °C
2.9 Compressive strength.
    | Compressive | Temperature | Age |
    | Strength |
    | ~80MPa | 23oC | 7Days |
    | ~50MPa | 30oC | 3Hours |
    | ~60MPa | 30oC | 4Hours |
    | ~62MPa | 30oC | 5Hours |
    | ~63MPa | 35oC | 3Hours |
    | ~66MPa | 35oC | 4Hours |
    | ~67MPa | 35oC | 5Hours |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: Standard: GB2567-
    Test method printed: 2008 (Cylinder-

2.10 Glass transition temperature.
    | Curing time | Curing temp. | TG |
    | 30 days | +30 °C | +58 °C |
    | 7 days | +30 °C | +60 °C |
    Test method printed: (EN 12614)

2.11 Heat deflection temperature.

    | 7 days | +35 °C | +53 °C |
    | Resistant to continuous exposure up to +45 °C. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (ASTM D 648)
2.12 System structure. Substrate primer - Sikadur®-330. Impregnating / laminating resin - Sikadur®-330. Structural strengthening fabric - SikaWrap® type to suit requirements.
2.13 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store in original, unopened, sealed and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.
2.14 Packaging.
    | 5 kg (A+B) | Pre-batched unit |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Substrate must be sound and of sufficient tensile strength to provide a minimum pull off strength of 1.0 N/mm² or as per the requirements of the design specification.
    - See also the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual dry application" Ref 850 41 02.
3.3 Substrate preparation. See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual dry application" Ref 850 41 02.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 04.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Component A : component B = 4 : 1 by weight; When using bulk material the exact mixing ratio must be safeguarded by accurately weighing and dosing each component.
    - Consumption: See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual dry application" Ref 850 41 02. Guide: 0.7 - 1.5 kg/m²
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Pot life | Open time |
    | +10 °C | ~90 minutes | ~90 minutes |
    | (5 kg) |
    | +23 °C | ~60 minutes | ~60 minutes |
    | (5 kg) |
    | +35 °C | ~30 minutes | ~30 minutes |
    | (5 kg) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 9514)
    Note printed: The pot life begins when the resin and hardener are mixed. It is shorter at high temperatures and longer at low temperatures. The greater the quantity mixed, the shorter the pot life. To obtain longer workability at high temperatures, the mixed adhesive may be divided into portions. Another method is to chill components A+B before mixing them (not below +5 °C).
4.4 Mixing - Pre-batched units. Mix components A+B together for at least 3 minutes with a mixing spindle attached to a slow speed electric drill (max. 300 rpm) until the material becomes smooth in consistency and a uniform grey colour. Avoid aeration while mixing. Then, pour the whole mix into a clean container and stir again for approx. 1 more minute at low speed to keep air entrapment at a minimum. Mix only that quantity which can be used within its pot life.
4.5 Mixing - Bulk packing, not pre-batched. First, stir each component thoroughly. Add the components in the correct proportions into a suitable mixing pail and stir correctly using an electric low speed mixer as above for pre-batched units.
4.6 Application method / tools. See the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual dry application" Ref 850 41 02.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all equipment immediately with Sika® Colma Cleaner. Cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikadur®-330 must be protected from rain for at least 24 hours after application.
    - Ensure placement of fabric and laminating with roller takes place within open time.
    - At low temperatures and / or high relative humidity, a tacky residue (blush) may form on the surface of the cured Sikadur®-330 epoxy. If an additional layer of fabric or a coating is to be applied onto the cured epoxy, this residue must first be removed with warm, soapy water to ensure adequate bond. In any case, the surface must be wiped dry prior to application of the next layer or coating.
    - For application in cold or hot conditions, pre-condition material for 24 hours in temperature controlled storage facilities to improve mixing, application and pot life limits.
    - For further information on over coating, number of layers or creep, please consult a structural engineer for calculations and see also the "Method Statement for SikaWrap® manual dry application" Ref 850 41 02. Sikadur® resins are formulated to have low creep under permanent loading. However due to the creep behaviour of all polymer materials under load, the long term structural design load must account for creep. Generally the long term structural design load must be lower than 20-25% of the failure load. Please consult a structural engineer for load calculations for the specific application.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Dew point. Beware of condensation. Substrate temperature during application must be at least 3 °C above dew point.
5.4 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.5 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % pbw
5.6 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Sikadur®-330 must be protected from rain for at least 24 hours after application.
    - At low temperatures and / or high relative humidity, a tacky residue (blush) may form on the surface of the cured Sikadur®-330 epoxy. If an additional layer of fabric or a coating is to be applied onto the cured epoxy, this residue must first be removed with warm, soapy water to ensure adequate bond. In any case, the surface must be wiped dry prior to application of the next layer or coating.
    - For application in cold or hot conditions, pre-condition material for 24 hours in temperature controlled storage facilities to improve mixing, application and pot life limits.
5.7 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Compressive | Temperature | Age; Strength; ~80MPa | 23oC | 7Days; ~50MPa | 30oC | 3Hours; ~60MPa | 30oC | 4Hours; ~62MPa | 30oC | 5Hours; ~63MPa | 35oC | 3Hours; ~66MPa | 35oC | 4Hours; ~67MPa | 35oC | 5Hours Standard: GB2567- 2008 (Cylinder- 10mm diameter* 25mm height) @23o C
    - Modulus of elasticity in flexure: ~ 3 800 N/mm² (7 days at +23 °C) (DIN EN 1465)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 30 N/mm² (7 days at +23°C) (ISO 527)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~ 4 500 N/mm² (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile strain at break: 0.9 % (7 days at +23 °C) (ISO 527)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: Concrete fracture (> 4 N/mm²) on sandblasted substrate (EN ISO 4624)
    - Coefficient of thermal expansion: 4.5 × 10⁻⁵ 1/K (Temperature range −10 °C − +40 °C) (EN 1770)
    - Glass transition temperature: Curing time | Curing temp. | TG; 30 days | +30 °C | +58 °C; 7 days | +30 °C | +60 °C (EN 12614) (ASTM D3418)
    - Heat deflection temperature: Curing time | Curing temperat- | HDT; ure; 7 days | +10 °C | +36 °C; 7 days | +23 °C | +47 °C; 7 days | +35 °C | +53 °C; Resistant to continuous exposure up to +45 °C. (ASTM D 648)
    - Pot Life: Temperature | Pot life | Open time; +10 °C | ~90 minutes | ~90 minutes; (5 kg); +23 °C | ~60 minutes | ~60 minutes; (5 kg); +35 °C | ~30 minutes | ~30 minutes; (5 kg) (EN ISO 9514)
5.8 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.9 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikadur®-330, May 2023, Version 04.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/sikadur_-330.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-330 Part A, version 16/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-sikadur-330parta.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikadur®-330 Part B, version 16/12/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sds-sikadur-330partb.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
